380YE Spring Equinox Announcement by the.d: At the Spring Equinox of 380YE the Civilian Commissioner of Dawn, using the power to commission constructions delegated by the Senate, approved the Gardens of Tiberius' Bequest, a small sinecure in Laroc, Astolat, that will produce Cerulean Mazzarine. The announcement did not specify the sinecure's size, so standard costs apply. After the Spring Equinox, Morien provided 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns towards the work. Once completed, the sinecure will automatically create the Dawnish national title of Healer of Dawn, to be assigned by the Dawnish Senators.

n.Dawn: Dawn gains a commissioned sinecure that, once completed, will create the national title of Healer of Dawn, appointed by its own Senators and supplied with Cerulean Mazzarine.

t.Astolat: The Gardens of Tiberius' Bequest are to be built in Laroc in Astolat, with Morien already contributing white granite and crowns towards their construction.

380YE Spring Equinox Announcement by the.d: Using the Senate's delegated power to commission constructions, the Highborn Civilian Commissioner approved Rhesa's announcement of a School of Exorcism in Tabernacle, Reikos. It cost 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns in labour, both supplied by Rhesa after the Spring Equinox, and would take three months to build. Once complete it creates the national title of Master of the School of Exorcism, a liao-producing sinecure that exists only because of a specific opportunity. The announcement intended election through the Highguard National Assembly, but the Commissioner's limited powers mean the title cannot be appointed that way unless a Senator raises a motion amending its method of appointment.

n.Highguard: Highguard gains a new national title, the Master of the School of Exorcism, though its appointment by the Highguard National Assembly would need a Senate motion amending the title's method of appointment.

t.Reikos: The School of Exorcism is to be built in Tabernacle, Reikos, using 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns over three months, and will produce liao once complete.

380YE Spring Equinox Announcement by the.d: Using the power to commission constructions delegated to them by the Senate, the Imperial Orc Civilian Commissioner approved a series of great drums in Estermark to aid the raising of Skarsind's cattle herds. The resulting sinecure, the Great Eastern Herd, produces 216 rings a season and is administered by the Shepherd of the Great Herd, a title appointed by unanimous decision of the Imperial Orc senators. The work cost 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns in labour, taking three months to build. Yargol provided the materials and funds after the Spring Equinox 380YE, and the Great Herd has since been completed.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs gained a new national title, the Shepherd of the Great Herd, appointed unanimously by their senators to oversee a sinecure worth 216 rings a season.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind's cattle herds are now supported by a series of great drums, forming the completed Great Eastern Herd sinecure.

r.Skarsind/Estermark: Estermark is the site of the great drums built to aid cattle-raising, now home to the completed Great Eastern Herd.

380YE Spring Equinox Announcement by the.d: Using the power to commission constructions delegated by the Senate, the Marcher Civilian Commissioner approved a sinecure in Graven, Gravenmarch, Bregasland, to produce mana crystals. The post, titled the Keeper of the Dour Fens, was to be appointed by vote of the Marcher farmers and held for life. The announcement came after the maximum number of commissions for the season had already been authorised, and was made in case one of the earlier commissions was vetoed by the Synod. No veto was used, so this commission was not authorised and the sinecure was not created.

n.The Marches: The Marcher Civilian Commissioner tried to create a lifetime post, the Keeper of the Dour Fens, chosen by the Marcher farmers, but the commission failed for lack of an available slot.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland was to gain a mana-producing sinecure, but the commission was not authorised and nothing was built.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Graven in Gravenmarch was the proposed site of the Keeper of the Dour Fens sinecure, which went unbuilt because the commission was not authorised.

380YE Spring Equinox Imperial elections.d: Five Senate seats were filled: Segura (incumbent), Karsk (Maarit), Reikos (Balthasar Suns of Couros), Holberg (Stern) and Feroz (Pedro i Taziel I Riqueza). Ambassadors, ministers and most national Civilian Commissioners were appointed. On the Military Council, Horsa Tyrshalt was revoked as General of the Fist of the Mountains for dereliction of duty and replaced by Erkenbrand. Several Synod positions changed hands. The incumbent Grandmaster of the Sevenfold Path was killed in battle and replaced by Zephaniah. In the Bourse, Syrene's Wisdom (155 thrones) and the Scorrero Nets (130 thrones) were auctioned, alongside other Imperial and national seats.

n.Dawn: Morien Stewart was named Civilian Commissioner of Dawn.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Reikos gained Balthasar Suns of Couros as senator, and Highborn took several Synod roles: Alys as Gatekeeper of Vigilance, Sariel as Virtue Inquisitor of Wisdom and Apollos as Curator of the White City Museum. The nation's Civilian Commissioner post was left unfilled.
n.Imperial Orcs: Bloodcrow Yargol was named Civilian Commissioner of the Imperial Orcs, and the incumbent Advisor on Orc Affairs kept the post.
n.Navarr: Bron Foxden was named Civilian Commissioner of Navarr.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast returned its incumbent senator for Segura, elected Pedro i Taziel I Riqueza for Feroz and saw Carlos I Guerra named Civilian Commissioner.
n.The League: Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg of the League was listed as Empress. Stern took the Senate seat for Holberg and Lorenzo of the Butchers became Civilian Commissioner of the League.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Civilian Commissioner of Urizen is listed with no holder named.
n.Varushka: Maarit became senator for Karsk, Nadya Gremani was named Civilian Commissioner of Varushka, and Wilhemina Maryenkovich Poltova of Varushka became Gatekeeper of Prosperity.
n.Wintermark: Thanmir Hrafnar was named Civilian Commissioner of Wintermark. Vauraus Korppitkotka became Virtue Inquisitor of Prosperity and Eldeen Wulfssdottir became Watcher of Britta's Pool.

t.Feroz: Pedro i Taziel I Riqueza was elected senator for Feroz.
t.Holberg: Stern was elected senator for Holberg.
t.Karsk: Maarit was elected senator for Karsk.
t.Reikos: Balthasar Suns of Couros was elected senator for Reikos.
t.Segura: Segura's incumbent senator was returned to the seat.

380YE Spring Equinox winds of fortune.d: Grendel orcs invaded Sarvos and began coordinated pillaging. Holberg's angry trees fell still, opening reclamation opportunities. Golan's Courage of the First Empress movement kept growing in Highguard. The eternal Janon opened a regio in Astolat, and the Asavean Plenum petitioned to build a temple on the Bay of Catazar. A harsh winter brought near-starvation to Skarsind, and meltwater now threatens flooding in the south. Dogri Thulebane offered to treat at Crow's Ridge, and a Freemoor village sought to reconnect with the Marches. Karsk's roads were completed and a third Varushkan army began mustering. Work was ordered or begun on a Sermersuaq mithril mine, a Kallavesa shrine and a second Mournwold fortification.

n.Dawn: The eternal Janon opened a regio in the woodlands of Astolat that mundanes as well as magicians may visit, and Golan's courage movement may spread into Dawn.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: a Druj diplomatic delegation was delayed by the Winter Solstice storms and is expected to attend at the Spring Equinox.
n.Grendel: Grendel orcs invaded the southern League city of Sarvos and appear to be carrying out widespread, well-coordinated pillaging.
n.Highguard: The preacher Golan's Courage of the First Empress movement kept gathering strength across Highguard, despite the efforts of the priests Yael and Nina.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skarsind suffered a dreadful winter with real risk of starvation, empty skies, and Dogri Thulebane's continued hold on Crow's Ridge, while the Senate commissioned mining and trade projects there.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: work on a second Mournwold fortification builds on a captured, partly finished Jotun fortification, and the Hearth Tithe herbs are meant to aid the war against them.
n.Navarr: A magical enchantment led Navarr ships into danger and rich booty. Trading posts were ordered for Hercynia, and Golan's courage movement may reach Navarr.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast faced storms, life-giving magical waters and the threat of spring flooding, and the Synod's dealings with the Hierro orcs in Segura changed significantly.
n.The League: The League saw Sarvos sacked by the Grendel and Holberg freed from its angry trees, with reclamation opportunities. Strange effects were reported around Tassato, floods threaten, and the vyig asset auction was rescheduled for Spring.
n.The Marches: After last year's failed harvest, the Marches faced a harsh winter, strange births and flooding along its rivers. A long-separated village in Freemoor reached out, and every farm continues the Hearth Tithe.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: a delayed Thule delegation is expected at the Spring Equinox, and the earlier peace treaty with the Thule enabled Varushkan public works.
n.Urizen: Urizen was tied to celestial omens and magical storms and waters. Covens of the Auric Horizon and Echostorm spire led Meraud's challenge with a fiftieth-magnitude ritual.
n.Varushka: Varushkan captains were drawn into enchanted voyages, and strange births were reported. Karsk's roads were completed and mustering of the Iron Helm army began, though the colleges in Volchitrava and Mieriada lagged.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's assembly largely failed to dislodge Dogri Thulebane from Crow's Ridge. Meanwhile a mithril mine was ordered in Sermersuaq, a shrine to Empress Britta begun in Kallavesa, and the Hearth Tithe continues.

t.Astolat: The eternal Janon, the Shadowed Flame, opened a regio in Astolat's woodlands and invited Imperial citizens, mundane and magician alike, to visit.
t.Bay of Catazar: Fog was reported on the brine, and the Asavean Plenum petitioned the Senate to build a temple on the Bay in exchange for an Imperial temple in Nemoria.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: severe weather in Casinea at the Winter Solstice kept several foreign delegations away, and they are expected at the Spring Equinox.
t.Hercynia: The Senate resolved to open trading offices and trading posts in Hercynia to begin establishing the "crossroads of the north".
t.Holberg: The angry trees that had assaulted Holberg for a year fell still, and the civil service assembled opportunities to repair the damage. The skies over Holberg remain strangely empty.
t.Kallavesa: Construction began on a major shrine to Empress Britta and a great work to draw pilgrims to the marshes where Wintermark heroes are laid to rest.
t.Karsk: The rebuilding of Karsk's roads was completed, boosting all its mines and forests, and mustering of the new Iron Helm army began there, likely to finish by Winter.
t.Miekarova: Construction began on the Hearth of the Tempest in Mieriada, though its progress is unclear and it is not yet working as a college of spring magic.
t.Mournwold: Work began on a second fortification using a captured, partly finished Jotun fortification, due shortly before the Summer Solstice if the Empire keeps the site. A Freemoor village also reached out to the Marches.
t.Sarvos: The Grendel invaded Sarvos and appear to be pillaging the city in a widespread, well-coordinated way.
t.Segura: The Synod's efforts to deal with the Hierro clan orcs in Segura saw the situation change significantly over the season.
t.Sermersuaq: The Senate ordered work on a new mithril mine in Sermersuaq, expected to be completed by the Autumn Equinox.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind endured a winter of near-starvation and empty skies, with Dogri Thulebane still holding Crow's Ridge. The Senate commissioned a ministry for human miners at Gulhule and new trading posts.
t.Tassato: Tassato was named in a roundup of magical and unusual effects across the Empire, which included warped skies and a crumbling castle.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: James Appleseeder of Upwold was named by the Marcher assembly to encourage the reintroduction of the Hearth Tithe.

r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Construction has begun on the Hearth of the Tempest in Mieriada, but it is not believed to be operating as a college of spring magic yet.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: The isolated village of Whittle in Freemoor reached out to its Marcher cousins after thirty years of separation, seeking to reconnect with the Empire.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Thane Dogri Thulebane continues to occupy Crow's Ridge despite Wintermark's efforts, and has offered a select few an invitation to treat with him.

380YE Spring Equinox winds of war.d: In Spiral, Dawnish, Urizen and other armies, aided by Spring healing magic and three thousand knights of Eleonaris, captured Cinion and Ankra after an eldritch wildfire. They also advanced on Ossuary. In Reikos, Navarr, Highborn and League forces cleared Grey Charge and part of Tamarbode. A Dawnish crusade held Dawnguard under a corrupting miasma. In the Mournwold, Jotun under a mandowla-skull banner held the line against nearly forty thousand Imperial soldiers, at heavy cost to both sides. The Jotun also secured Liathaven, took half of West Marsh, and seized Serra Damata and part of Serra Briante. The Grendel, hidden by the Catazar fog, conquered Cigno, looted Sarvos and struck at Glass Point. Agents of the Queen of Silence gathered the fallen.

n.Dawn: The Hounds of Glory and Eastern Sky led the assaults that took Cinion and Ankra, joined by three thousand angry knights of Eleonaris whose presence magistrates are likely to investigate. The Golden Sun's crusade, swelled by some six thousand Dawnish troops, held Dawnguard against the Barrens orcs.
n.Druj: In Reikos, scattered barbarian orcs were driven from most of Grey Charge but still held parts of Tamarbode. The lingering aura of fear left by the Druj helped slow the Imperial advance.
n.Grendel: The Grendel lost Cinion and Ankra and were pushed back towards Ossuary, despite skilful, supernaturally coordinated defence. Their surprise naval invasion took Cigno and the city of Sarvos, looted its riches and pushed into Uccelini.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar helped clear Grey Charge in Reikos, clashing with League looters over the plunder. Highborn forces joined the failed assault on the Jotun castle at Sarcombe, and Jotun looting in Serra Damata took white granite that might have gone to Jeremiah of the Cenotaph.
n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc forces fought savagely in the Mournwold, with the Winter Sun killing captured Jotun and the Summer Storm slaughtering all in their way, yet they gained no ground. One band of Imperial Orcs joined the crusade in Dawnguard.
n.Jotun: The Jotun held every inch of the Mournwold at a cost of at least six thousand warriors, secured Liathaven uncontested, and conquered about half of West Marsh. They also seized Serra Damata and a fifth of Serra Briante, smashing a frozen citadel and plundering mines.
n.Navarr: The Quiet Step led the overwhelming assault in Reikos, and Navarr raiders burned Barrens orc villages, likely ending any hope of a Navarr–Barrens alliance. Liathaven fell silent under Jotun control, and settlements of displaced Navarr in Kahraman were destroyed without mercy.
n.The Brass Coast: The Fire in the South fled Liathaven to fight in the Mournwold, while the Red Wind Corsairs plundered Jotun encampments there. At home, some thirty thousand Jotun invaded Kahraman, taking Serra Damata and part of Serra Briante.
n.The League: The League suffered a shock as Grendel seized Sarvos and looted its university, cathedral, banks and the tomb of Empress Giselle. They also struck at Glass Point. Elsewhere the Wolves of War plundered orc strongholds in Reikos, the Towerjacks helped defend Dawnguard, and work began on the College of the Liberated in Bocche.
n.The Marches: After a disastrous harvest the Marches endured a hungry winter. Its forces joined the assault on Sarcombe, but no Mournish soil was regained. The Marchers hold a fortification on the Greensward and have begun a second castle in Ore Hills.
n.Urizen: The Citadel Guard fought at the heart of the Spiral campaign without a single fatality and were untouched by the wildfire. The servants of the Queen of Silence found none to claim from among them. Redoubt was harried by Grendel guerrillas but protected by a healing enchantment.
n.Wintermark: A Jotun force from the west conquered about half of West Marsh, offering halls the choice of joining them or thraldom. They are now threatening Westerhal and potentially Rundahl beyond.

t.Bay of Catazar: Magical storms rolled off the bay without breaking its preternatural fog. That fog then cloaked the Grendel fleet that invaded Sarvos.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks of Holberg fought in Dawnguard, and Holberg's soldiers recognised the Barrens curse from long experience.
t.Kahraman: Some thirty thousand Jotun poured in from Liathaven, seizing Serra Damata and a fifth of Serra Briante. Magical citadels slowed their advance.
t.Kallavesa: Jotun forces landed on the western coast and conquered about half of West Marsh. They are establishing supply lines into the territory.
t.Liathaven: The Jotun secured the whole forest uncontested despite clashes with mysterious pale legionaries. A grim silence fell, and no more Navarr refugees came south.
t.Mournwold: Three months of slaughter against an unyielding Jotun line left the Empire with no gains. Nearly three thousand Imperial troops and at least twice as many Jotun fell.
t.Redoubt: Remnant Grendel guerrillas ambushed Imperial armies and wrecked roads and bridges. A Spring healing enchantment on the territory blunted the casualties.
t.Reikos: Imperial armies cleared most orcs from Grey Charge and advanced in Tamarbode, but at least another season is needed to complete the liberation.
t.Sarvos: A surprise Grendel invasion conquered Cigno and the jewelled city and looted its treasures. The Grendel also pushed into Uccelini, while work on the College of the Liberated began in Bocche.
t.Spiral: Under healing waters and sea-storms, the Empire retook Cinion and Ankra and advanced on Ossuary. A wildfire destroyed Ossen's Spire, and fleets based in Spiral suffered a small penalty from the storms.
t.The Barrens: In Dawnguard, Imperial defenders held off a desperate Barrens orc assault under a corrupting crimson miasma. The orcs still control a portion of the region.

r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: A second ice-and-granite citadel, supported by troops from Fort Braydon, halted the Jotun short of the Great Mine and Briante. The Jotun still took about a fifth of the region.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: The Jotun smashed a frozen citadel and claimed the Damatian Cliffs, the town of Damata and the orichalcum mines. They also plundered white granite from the quarries.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: The Jotun conquered about half the region, giving each hall a choice of warrior service or thraldom. Westerhal is their next target.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: Imperial forces struck at the Jotun in Freemoor but made no headway against the mandowla-banner line.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Mentioned in passing: the Marchers control a fortification on the Greensward.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Mentioned in passing: work has begun on a second Marcher castle here, following an earlier Jotun defeat in the region.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Highborn and Marcher forces brought siege engines against the Jotun castle in the ruins of Sarcombe but failed to take any ground.
r.Reikos/Grey Charge: Imperial armies cleared most of the orcs from the ruins of the fallen chapter houses and conquered the region.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Significant headway was made, but parts of the region, especially the Sign of Tamar, remain in barbarian hands.
r.Sarvos/Bocche: Work began near Trivento on the College of the Liberated, which some say is meant to revitalise the fading town.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: The Grendel conquered the island and the city of Sarvos within a week. They looted Diora University, the Capodomus cathedral and the tomb of Empress Giselle, but left the embassies alone.
r.Sarvos/Uccelini: Grendel forces bypassed fortified estates to fight for the docks of Glass Point, making significant headway towards conquering the isles.
r.Spiral/Ankra: After brutal fighting below Ossen's Spire, the Empire captured Ankra. The Spire was consumed by eldritch fire and Damakan's Forge badly damaged.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Mentioned in passing: great storm-driven waves battered its coast.
r.Spiral/Ateri: Storms beat against its cliffs while a frozen citadel garrisoned by one-eyed giants watched for Grendel aggression from its hills.
r.Spiral/Cinion: The Empire took Cinion after a wildfire killed nearly a thousand and stripped its slopes of trees and heather.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Imperial forces made significant headway towards recapturing the mithril mines here.
r.Spiral/Screed: Mentioned in passing: the Dawnish avoided Screed and the black behemoth at its heart.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: The Golden Sun's crusade held Dawnguard against a desperate orc assault under a festering miasma. The Towers of the Dawn absorbed heavy damage, and the orcs still hold part of the region.

A fundamental struggle (Trade Winds).d: Sumaah diplomats kept denouncing the Synod as heretics, slowly souring foreign views of the Imperial Way. An Ambassador to the Sumaah was to be appointed. Asavean relations had recovered after the trade-ban law was abrogated, though the Tarquinius family still sought retribution. An Imperial embassy opened in Leerdam, but the Commonwealth, troubled by Imperial ambiguity on slavery, searched ships, ended crystal mana sales and cheapened Artisan's Oil. Jarm's House of Princes lifted its crystal mana embargo, and Rigia became a fully functioning port offering good green iron deals. Sarcophan stayed neutral. Regario Dossier agents became active in Robec, Issyk, Kantor and Faraden.

n.Dawn: A Dawnish captain, Gerralt, illustrates the new Commonwealth regime, enduring a search for slaves and contraband in Leerdam while carrying Dawnish wood, wine, brandy and true vervain.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Sarcophan Delves are said to welcome even the Grendel to their port.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the completed Sumaah embassy in Necropolis has not ended the Republic's war with the Empire.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Meade and Siroc are named among the ports from which Imperial captains set sail.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos and Tassato are named as ports for Imperial captains, and the Commonwealth embassy stands in the City of a Thousand Sails.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Lacre is named among the Imperial ports from which fleets sail.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Korotny is named among the Imperial ports from which fleets sail.
n.Wintermark: Stormcrow Beodun Snowlock of Wintermark, sent by the Synod at Prince Barbara Radz's invitation, countered Sumaah anti-Imperial preaching in the Eastern Principalities of Jarm with some success, helping win the princes' goodwill.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: wine and brandy from Astolat's vineyards form part of Captain Gerralt's cargo searched in Leerdam.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan ships are regular visitors to the ports of the Bay of Catazar, where trade remains healthy.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: its port of Korotny is listed among those from which Imperial captains set sail.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named directly, but Brass Coast ports such as Siroc are listed among those from which Imperial captains sail.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: its port of Lacre is listed among those from which Imperial captains set sail.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the Sumaah embassy here has been completed, yet the Republic remains at war with the Empire.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is named as a sailing port, and the Commonwealth embassy in the City of a Thousand Sails has been completed.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; it is at most implied among the smaller Imperial ports from which captains sail.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is named among the ports from which Imperial captains set sail.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: hardwood from Weirwater's forests is part of Captain Gerralt's cargo inspected in Leerdam.

A throne of blood.d: A Navarri messenger was told by Dogri's Crowskeepers that Dogri would talk, but only at Crowskeep in Crow's Ridge. Kali of the Saker had to attend, accompanied only by Skarsind folk, and a former senator was barred. Breaking the terms would end the meeting, and Dogri would defend his borders against anyone. The Wintermark national assembly's Winter Solstice statement urged Winterfolk not to join Dogri. Some stubborn Winterfolk left Skarsind, but die-hards went north to him. The Four Seasons Market stayed in Wintermark hands because no Imperial Orc came to claim it. The civil service confirmed a Sentinel Gate conjunction to Crowskeep at the Spring Equinox.

n.Imperial Orcs: While the orcs build their nation in southern Skarsind, the Four Seasons Market remains in Wintermark hands, because its owner says no Imperial Orc came to take it over.
n.Wintermark: The assembly's call to come home persuaded some Winterfolk to leave Skarsind, but die-hards joined Dogri, who demanded that Kali of the Saker and Skarsind folk meet him at Crowskeep.

t.Skarsind: The territory remained divided, with the Imperial Orcs building in the south and Dogri's Winterfolk rebels holding the north as spring brought new recruits to his banner.

r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Dogri's forces still held Crow's Ridge, and he named Crowskeep as the only place he would meet, reachable through a Sentinel Gate conjunction at the Spring Equinox.

Across the seven seas.d: The in-character story has the Freeborn painter Mirkala, at Siroc, telling children about the seven seas: Sighs, Teeth, Storms, Salt, Steel, Snow and a mysterious seventh sea of starlight. Enchanted fleets ran into mist-shrouded islands with unliving courtiers, a pig-obsessed Night magician, helpful dolphins, an angry pirate, a ghost ship of dead Sarcophan to be beaten in a rhyming contest, dodos guarding tempest jade, an ambergris-spewing whale and a giant sea turtle mistaken for an island. Overcoming these challenges brought extra wealth and tales to tell in Anvil. Rhianos appears to be a Summer eternal. Imperial scholars know little of them, and the Empire has had no significant dealings with them for centuries.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: in Mirkala's story, sailors returning through the Sea of Sighs are relieved to be nearly home, provided they can get past the Grendel.
n.Navarr: All fleets owned by Navarr characters were enchanted, so captains who traded abroad or went privateering met strange maritime adventures and earned additional booty.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Mirkala describes the Sea of Snow stretching past Otkodov, 'where the wicked Thule live', and claims no ships sail it because of ice and the dark magic of the dragon princes.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Mirkala jokes that the Sea of Storms is deep enough to swallow the mountains of Urizen, with wizards bobbing up complaining about their ruined silk robes.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Mirkala describes the Bay as only the northernmost part of the Sea of Sighs.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Mirkala's tale has the Sea of Snow stretching past Otkodov, home of the Thule.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: in Mirkala's story it is the ice-filled sixth sea, rumoured to hold strange beasts such as horned whales and giant tusked seals, and said to be shunned by ships because of the ice and the Thule's magic.

Allocate Great Forest.d: Proposed by the senator for Reikos and seconded by the senator for Astolat on the virtue of Prosperity, the motion sought to make the Great Forest, a bourse seat in Reikos, a national position appointed by Highguard. The Senate rejected it. A later motion to allocate the Great Forest as an Imperial position was passed, so the seat was not reserved for Highguard.

n.Highguard: Highguard failed to secure the Great Forest as a national bourse position, and the seat instead became an Imperial position under a subsequent motion.

t.Reikos: The Great Forest bourse seat in Reikos was not made a Highborn national position. It was allocated as an Imperial position by a later motion.

Allocate Great Forest II.d: Proposed by the senator for Bastion and seconded by Necropolis, the motion assigned the Great Forest of Peythat, the bourse seat in Reikos, as an Imperial Bourse Seat. It followed a previous motion to allocate the seat as a national position, which had failed. With this motion passed, the Great Forest became an Imperial seat and was due to be auctioned, for a reduced term, at the Summer Solstice 380YE.

n.Highguard: Highguard senators for Bastion and Necropolis proposed and seconded the motion, settling the bourse seat in Highguard-held Reikos as an Imperial position open to auction rather than a national one.

t.Reikos: The Great Forest bourse seat in Reikos became an Imperial position, due for auction for a reduced term at the Summer Solstice 380YE.

Appoint Commonwealth ambassador.d: This administrative motion created the first appointment of an Imperial Ambassador to the Commonwealth. The holder is responsible for the Commonwealth Embassy and represents the Empire in its dealings with the Commonwealth. The motion was carried, and Beatrix Amalia Novarian Zu Holberg was appointed to the position, becoming the Empire's first envoy to the Commonwealth.

n.The League: A citizen bearing the name Zu Holberg, Beatrix Amalia Novarian, became the Empire's first Ambassador to the Commonwealth, placing the League's diplomatic voice at the forefront of Imperial dealings with that nation.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg appears only in the name of the newly appointed ambassador, Beatrix Amalia Novarian Zu Holberg.

Appoint Throne V.d: The motion sought to elect a citizen to the Throne. Four nominees stood: Lisabetta von Holberg; Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason, Senator for Sermersuaq; Cyrus son of Felix, of Felix's Watch, the Imperial Magus; and Olle Markusson, Senator for Kallavesa. The campaign ended with Lisabetta von Holberg elected to the Throne, and the motion was afterwards ratified by Empress Lisabetta herself in Spring 380YE.

n.Wintermark: Two of Wintermark's senators, Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason and Olle Markusson, stood for the Throne but lost to Lisabetta von Holberg.

t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa's senator, Olle Markusson, was nominated for the Throne but was not elected.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq's senator, Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason, was nominated for the Throne but was not elected.

Archive:380YE Spring Equinox Imperial ti.d: The record lists the Empress, every territorial senator, Senate appointees, commissioners and sinecures, the generals of each nation's armies, the Synod's cardinals, gatekeepers and virtue inquisitors, the Conclave's archmagi and grandmasters, and the Bourse seats with their winning bids. It notes that Senator Dušan of Miekarova was revoked by the Synod but re-elected. The Civilian Commissioners of Urizen and Wintermark, the Dean of Pilgrims and the Imperial Fleet Master were vacant. The Great Pits of Ennerlund were being repaired, with mithril expected shortly after the Summer Solstice. The Great Forest at Reikos was due for auction at that Solstice. The Legacy was held by the Grendel, and the Stonefield Ice Caves by the Thule.

n.Dawn: Dawn held the senatorships of Astolat, Semmerholm and Weirwater, four generals (Hounds of Glory, Golden Sun, Eastern Sky and Gryphon's Pride), and the Cardinals of Pride and Wisdom.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are noted as holding the Legacy, which will be allocated when Spiral is once again an Imperial territory.
n.Highguard: Highguard held four senatorships, three generals (Seventh Wave, Granite Pillar and Valiant Pegasus), the Cardinals of Courage and Loyalty, and many Synod posts including Auditor of Senatorial Accountability.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs held Skarsind's senatorship through Irontide Vio, two generals (Winter Sun and Summer Storm), the Cardinal of the Way, the Conscience of the Senate and the Steel Fist.
n.Navarr: Navarr held three senatorships and two generals (Black Thorns and Quiet Step), and Brendan Brackensong served as Quartermaster General of the Imperial Armies.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast held four senatorships, two generals and an admiral of the Freeborn Storm, plus the Broken Shore Bounty and several sinecures.
n.The League: The League held the Throne through Empress Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, four senatorships, two generals, the Cardinals of Ambition, Prosperity and Vigilance, and the Imperial Inquisitor.
n.The Marches: The Marches held the senatorships of Bregasland, Mitwold and Upwold and four generals (Cullachs of the Tusks, Drakes, Strong Reeds and Bounders).
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are noted as holding Wintermark's Stonefield Ice Caves Bourse position.
n.Urizen: Urizen held three senatorships and one general of the Citadel Guard, but its Civilian Commissioner post was vacant.
n.Varushka: Varushka held four senatorships and two generals (Northern Eagle and Golden Axe), and its Miekarova senator Dušan was re-elected after a Synod revocation.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark held three senatorships and two generals (Green Shield and Fist of the Mountain), but its Civilian Commissioner post was vacant and its Stonefield Ice Caves were in Thule hands.

t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Ranulf Pridestalker is listed as Senator for Hercynia.
t.Holberg: Stern was Holberg's senator and the Empress came from Holberg, while the Great Pits of Ennerlund were being repaired, with mithril expected after the Summer Solstice.

t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Llewellyn Leafstalker is listed as Senator for Miaren.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova's senator Dušan Otecovna Zlata was revoked by the Synod but re-elected, and cannot be revoked again until after the next regular election.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Bridget Eastville is listed as Senator for Mitwold, Pride of the Marches.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Ariadne is listed as Senator for Morrow.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Ianthe of Raven's Watch is listed as Senator for Necropolis.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Probus of Shattered Spire is listed as Senator for Redoubt.
t.Reikos: Balthasar of the Suns of Couros was Reikos's senator, and the Great Forest at Reikos was due to be auctioned for a reduced term at the Summer Solstice.

t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra is listed as Senator for Segura.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Escalade Carsenere is listed as Senator for Semmerholm.

t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Legacy is noted as held by the Grendel until Spiral is once again an Imperial territory, and Damian is listed as Castellan of Spiral Castle.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Cesare Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato is listed as Senator for Tassato.

t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Caerwyn Summer Crow is listed as Senator for Therunin.
