r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The Great Pits of Ennerlund were under repair and expected to produce their first load of mithril shortly after the Summer Solstice 380YE.

Blossoms a rose in the deeps of my heart.d: A woodsman in the darkening Rosered Woods, south-east of Laroc, met a herald of Janon and the first of its knights, who charged him to carry an invitation. Janon intended to open the night-aligned regio at the heart of the woods, known as the Snowdrop Glade, so that non-magicians could attend. Night magicians, artists and priests were specifically invited. Performers, food and drink, contests and petitioners seeking boons were welcomed. The 'prince of toads', likely Sadogua, was expected to attend. A magician still had to open the Sentinel Gate, and visitors who could not open portals themselves would leave the chamber only at the eternal's sufferance.

n.Dawn: Janon's court was to be held within a Dawnish territory near Laroc, and the eternal's call for artists, performers and passionate petitioners offered Dawn's people a chance to seek its favour.

t.Astolat: Strange fires and a deepening gloom were reported in Astolat's Rosered Woods, where Janon planned to open the night regio to visitors arriving through the Sentinel Gate.

Construct Asavean Temple.d: Proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Madruga, the motion passed and the Asaveans began building the temple in the port-town of Oran on Feroz's northern coast, with six months expected for construction. When complete, the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull will create a non-Imperial title responsible for liaising with its priests. The Asaveans said they would be guided in that appointment by the Senator for Feroz. The Imperial Synod cannot revoke the title, though the priesthood may refuse to deal with a liaison. Completion was first expected before the Autumn Equinox 380YE, but significant delays fostered by Synod interference pushed it back to shortly before the Spring Equinox 381YE.

n.The Brass Coast: A Brass Coast territory became host to a foreign major temple, and the Senator for Feroz was given the say over who would serve as the temple's liaison.

t.Feroz: Feroz is the site of the Asavean Temple of Balo and the Black Bull, and its Senator will guide the Asaveans in appointing the temple's liaison.

r.Feroz/Oranseri: The Asaveans began building the temple in Oran, the bustling port-town on Feroz's northern coast, though Synod-fostered delays put its completion back to shortly before the Spring Equinox 381YE.

Construct Aurelie's Garden.d: Proposed by the senator for Weirwater and seconded by the senator for Sarvos, the motion created a self-funded herb garden sinecure near the hospital Aurelie's Rest in Grovesyard, Miaren. Its holder is to be decided by an annual contest of ten Dawnish against ten Navarr, using all skills until one team remains standing, with any further rules agreed between the teams. The motion passed. Construction was underway, with 10 weirwood and 20 crowns spent by Nym after the Spring Equinox. When complete it will create the Imperial title Keeper of Aurelie's Garden. The size of the sinecure, the term of the title and which Synod assemblies may revoke it were left for the senator to decide.

n.Dawn: Dawnish champions will field a team of ten in an annual contest against the Navarr to win control of the new herb garden sinecure.
n.Navarr: The Navarr gain a herb garden within their own territory of Miaren, but must defend control of it each year in a ten-against-ten contest with Dawn.

t.Miaren: A herb garden sinecure was ordered to be built in Grovesyard, beside the hospital Aurelie's Rest, and construction had begun with materials and funds committed.

Construct Ossuary of Reikos.d: Proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by the senator for Reikos on the virtue of prosperity, the motion commissioned a great work costing 40 wains of white granite, 40 wains of weirwood and 20 thrones in labour, taking a year to construct. The materials and money were provided by Ianthe after the Spring Equinox 380YE. Once complete, the ossuary was to grant 1300 rings split between the congregations of Reikos. Work on the Grand Ossuary was finished shortly before the Spring Equinox 381YE began.

n.Highguard: Highguard's senators for Necropolis and Reikos brought forward the ossuary, which will let thousands of highborn dead be laid to rest and add 1300 rings to the congregations of a Highborn-held territory.

t.Reikos: Reikos gained the Grand Ossuary, completed shortly before Spring 381YE, which lays its many dead to rest, enables the territory's rebuilding and grants 1300 rings to its congregations.

Construct the Blood Red Roads.d: Proposed by Tassato and seconded by Casinea, the motion set the cost at 360 wains of white granite and 90 thrones, with two years' construction. The roads would first connect the League cities of Temeschwar, Sarvos, Tassato and Holberg with Anvil and the territories of Casinea, Astolat and Semmerholm, then extend to Upwold, Hahnmark, Miaren, Karov and Madruga. Lorenzo La Volpe supplied materials in three instalments after Spring 380YE, Autumn 380YE and Spring 381YE, totalling 360 wains and 90 thrones. Work has begun and specialists are looking at speeding it up. When completed, farms and businesses in territories along the network will see increased income.

n.Dawn: Astolat and Semmerholm are among the first territories to be linked to Anvil and the League cities, so Dawnish farms and businesses there stand to earn more once the roads are complete.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Casinea seconded the motion and lies on the first stage of the network, promising higher income for its farms and businesses on completion.
n.Navarr: Navarr's Miaren is slated for connection in the network's later stage, which would raise income for farms and businesses there once built.
n.The Brass Coast: Madruga is to be reached in the second stage of the roads, giving Brass Coast farms and businesses there a future boost to income.
n.The League: The League drove the project: Tassato proposed it, Lorenzo La Volpe oversees it, Temeschwar's Bloody Butchers Guild funds it, and all four League cities form the network's core.
n.The Marches: Upwold is due to be connected in the later stage, which would raise income for Marcher farms and businesses there on completion.
n.Varushka: Karov is among the territories to be connected in the second stage, promising increased income for its farms and businesses once finished.
n.Wintermark: Hahnmark is to be joined to the network in its later stage, which would boost income for Wintermark farms and businesses there.

t.Astolat: Astolat is part of the first stage linking the League cities to Anvil, and its farms and businesses will earn more once the roads are complete.
t.Casinea: Casinea's senator seconded the motion, and the territory sits on the first stage of the roads, set to benefit from increased farm and business income.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark is to be connected in the network's subsequent stage, bringing higher income to its farms and businesses on completion.
t.Holberg: The city of Holberg is one of the four League cities at the heart of the first stage of the road network.
t.Karov: Karov is scheduled to join the network in its later stage, with increased farm and business income to follow on completion.
t.Madruga: Madruga is among the territories to be reached in the second stage, set to see higher income for its farms and businesses.
t.Miaren: Miaren is to be linked in the later stage of the roads, raising income for its farms and businesses once built.
t.Sarvos: The city of Sarvos is one of the League cities the roads first connect to Anvil and the neighbouring territories.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm is on the first stage of the network, and its farms and businesses will gain income when the roads are complete.
t.Tassato: Tassato's senator proposed the motion, and the city is one of the four League hubs at the centre of the first stage.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's Bloody Butchers Guild self-funds the Great Work, and the city is a core hub of the first stage of the roads.
t.Upwold: Upwold is to be connected in the subsequent stage, bringing increased income for its farms and businesses on completion.

Construct the Ministry of Industry and S.d: Proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Madruga, the motion took advantage of an opportunity to improve the wealth of Skarsind by raising a new ministry in Temeschwar, forming part of the greater Torfast ministries. Construction required 8 wains of white granite and 2 thrones in labour, and three months to build. Gant Archama provided the full cost after the Spring Equinox 380YE. The finished building was named the Northern Traders Guild and stands in Temeschwar city proper, in the region of Hanuri.

n.Imperial Orcs: The ministry was intended to improve the wealth of Skarsind, the Imperial Orc territory whose trade it was built to serve.
n.The League: The League gained a new ministry, the Northern Traders Guild, in its city of Temeschwar, adding to the Torfast ministries there.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind's trade and wealth were the purpose of the ministry, although the building itself was raised in Temeschwar rather than in Skarsind.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar became home to the Ministry of Industry and Skarsind Trade, built as the Northern Traders Guild among the greater Torfast ministries.

r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: The Northern Traders Guild was built in Temeschwar city proper, within Hanuri, once Gant Archama had supplied the white granite and labour costs.

Construct the Park of Holberg.d: Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by Feroz, the motion took up the opportunity to clear the ruined Holmauer and create space for parks. It cost 60 wains of weirwood, 40 wains of white granite and 25 Thrones in labour, with nine months of construction. Materials came from several donors: Othello von Holberg after the Autumn Equinox 380YE, Irina Kardaovich after the Winter Solstice 380YE, and Caerwynn von Holberg and Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar after the Autumn Equinox 381YE. Holmauer Park was finished shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE.

n.The League: League citizens proposed and largely paid for the work, with Othello and Caerwynn von Holberg among the donors, and the League city of Holberg gained Holmauer Park.

t.Holberg: Holberg's senator proposed the motion, the work was meant to be self-funded by the city's citizens, and Holberg gained a new park built on cleared ruins.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: The ruins of the Holmauer were cleared and restored, and Holmauer Park was completed there shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE.

Construct the expansion of Spiral Castle.d: The motion commissioned an expansion of Spiral Castle in Weirwater. Before it, the castle's resupply covered only Weirwater. Afterwards, the Castellan of Spiral Castle could use their power of resupply on any army that spent the entire season in Weirwater, Karsk, Karov, Astolat or Semmerholm. The motion was proposed by the senator for Astolat and seconded by the senator for Tassato, and it passed. The expansion raised the castle's upkeep from 7 to 10 Thrones per season.

n.Dawn: Dawn's senator for Astolat proposed the expansion, which extended the castle's resupply to armies spending a full season in the Dawnish territories of Weirwater, Astolat and Semmerholm.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is linked only through Spiral, the territory it held, which shares its name with Spiral Castle in Weirwater; the motion does not otherwise concern Grendel.
n.Varushka: Armies spending a full season in the Varushkan territories of Karov and Karsk came within reach of the Castellan of Spiral Castle's resupply.

t.Astolat: Astolat's senator proposed the motion, and armies spending the whole season in Astolat could now be resupplied by the Castellan of Spiral Castle.
t.Karov: Karov was one of the territories adjacent to Weirwater where armies spending the whole season could now be resupplied from Spiral Castle.
t.Karsk: Karsk was one of the territories adjacent to Weirwater where armies spending the whole season could now be resupplied from Spiral Castle.
t.Semmerholm: Armies spending the whole season in Semmerholm came within the expanded resupply reach of Spiral Castle's Castellan.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is linked only through the name of Spiral Castle, which stands in Weirwater; the motion does not concern the territory of Spiral itself.
t.Weirwater: Spiral Castle in Weirwater was expanded, extending its Castellan's resupply from Weirwater to its neighbouring territories and raising its upkeep from 7 to 10 Thrones per season.

Construct vale in Karsk.d: The motion called for a new vale to be built at the site of Ivarsgard in the Lestazny region of Karsk, taking the form of a self-funded folly at standard costs. After the Spring Equinox, Maarit Akkova Cendro provided 10 wains of white granite, 10 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones towards the work. The majority of the basic construction of the new vale of Ivarsgard was then completed, and the civil service began investigating what help it could offer to the exiles of Ivarsgard who wish to return to their rejuvenated vale.

n.Varushka: Varushka gains a rebuilt vale at Ivarsgard, largely funded by Maarit Akkova Cendro, and the vale's exiles may now be helped by the civil service to return home.

t.Karsk: Most of the basic construction of the new vale of Ivarsgard in Lestazny, Karsk, has been completed, opening the way for its exiles to return.

Conversion of Overton Garrison.d: Proposed by the senator for Upwold and seconded by Bregasland's, the motion passed at no cost. The garrison had become obsolete after Orchard's Watch was completed, and was disbanded. The conversion was due to be finished by the Summer Solstice 380YE. The new sinecure would then automatically create the annual Marcher national title of Sheriff of Overton, chosen by a vote of Marcher farmers at the Anvil Summit and revocable by the Marcher national assembly. The Sheriff's purpose was to stem banditry and raiding against the Mournwold mines and recover ore, though it remained unclear which ores would be recovered.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named on the page; they appear only because they held part of the Mournwold that season.
n.The Marches: The Marches gained a new annual national title, the Sheriff of Overton, elected by Marcher farmers and answerable to the Marcher national assembly. The Sheriff was charged with protecting the Mournwold mines from bandits and raiders.

t.Mournwold: Overton's obsolete garrison was disbanded and its site turned into The Sheriff's House, which aimed to stem raiding on the territory's mines and reclaim their ore.

r.Mournwold/Greensward: Overton in Greensward became home to The Sheriff's House, the seat of the new Marcher Sheriff of Overton, replacing the disbanded garrison there.

Dark skies.d: Astronomancers in Urizen, Varushka and the Brass Coast reported a new star, invisible to the naked eye, following the Wanderer; the Conclave has not named it, and some mystics link it to the unnamed rune. Scholars of the Observatory of the Blazing Mirror in Iteri, aided by Camillius of Endsmeet, built a device to study it, housed in the new Camillius Steeple, to be unveiled at the Spring Equinox. The Phoenix is waning, making its magic and arcane projections harder, except for Winterfolk. Psychological ailments keep climbing, with tragedies in Bregasland, Temeschwar and Kallavesa. Over Skarsind and Holberg the night sky is empty, and naga who dwell there grow markedly more secretive.

n.Imperial Orcs: The night skies over Skarsind, the Imperial Orcs' new homeland, have become entirely empty save for the moon, an unexplained phenomenon unlike the Penumbral Veil.
n.The League: Holberg's night skies have vanished, and in Temeschwar a troupe master slew his entire cast during a production of "The Swords of Absalom", raving about ghosts of dead actors possessing the living.
n.The Marches: A Bregasland fendweller imprisoned two neighbours in a lightless pit as part of an incomprehensible study of fear, one sign of the mania spreading through the Empire.
n.Urizen: Urizen astronomancers helped sight the new star, and the Observatory of the Blazing Mirror in Iteri built the Camillius Steeple to study it, with an unveiling planned for the Spring Equinox.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: astronomancers from Varushkan observatories were among those who reported sighting the new star.
n.Wintermark: Winterfolk magicians alone can create arcane projections without the extra effort the fading Phoenix imposes, for reasons no one understands, while a circle of Kallavesi mystics poisoned themselves in their marshes.

t.Bregasland: A fendweller imprisoned two of her neighbours in a lightless pit as part of a bizarre study of fear.
t.Holberg: The night skies over the recently liberated city are entirely empty save for the moon, and naga who spend long periods there find their secretiveness greatly strengthened.
t.Kallavesa: A circle of Kallavesi mystics poisoned themselves in the marshes, leaving a hastily scrawled note about their intention to "merge with the cosmos".
t.Skarsind: The night skies over the Imperial Orcs' new homeland are empty but for the moon, and naga who dwell there long grow compulsively secretive.
t.Temeschwar: A production of "The Swords of Absalom" ended in tragedy when the troupe master was found to have slain the entire cast.
t.Zenith: Zenith is home to the Observatory of the Blazing Mirror, whose scholars built a device to study the new star in the newly named Camillius Steeple.

r.Zenith/Iteri: The Observatory of the Blazing Mirror in Iteri constructed the Camillius Steeple to examine the new star, with Arbiter Horace inviting Camillius of Endsmeet to give the keynote at its Spring Equinox unveiling, which archmages and grandmasters were expected to attend.

Disburse funds for Pilgrim's Trail.d: Proposed by the senator for Kallavesa and seconded by the senator for Redoubt, this motion followed an earlier motion that had commissioned the Pilgrim's Trail as a great work. It sought additional funds of 18 Thrones to purchase the resources needed for construction of the pilgrim trails in Kallavesa. The motion was passed in principle and then passed at 18 Thrones, and the money was disbursed to the senator for Kallavesa.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark's senator for Kallavesa secured 18 Thrones from the Imperial treasury to help build the Pilgrim's Trail in Wintermark lands.

t.Kallavesa: The 18 Thrones were disbursed to Kallavesa's senator to buy the resources needed to construct the pilgrim trails in the territory.

Disburse funds for resupply III.d: The motion sought Senate money for the resupply of the Imperial armies and was put forward by the senator for Bregasland, with Mitwold seconding. It passed in principle and was set at 250 thrones, which were disbursed to Senator Bregasland. The page notes that the motion did not give the senator the power to carry out emergency resupply of the armies themselves, so the funds were handed over without that authority attached.

n.The Marches: Two Marcher senators, from Bregasland and Mitwold, proposed and seconded the motion, and 250 thrones of Senate money went into the hands of the Marches' senator for Bregasland.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland's senator proposed the motion and received the 250 thrones disbursed for resupplying the armies, though without power to perform emergency resupply.

Disburse funds to citizens of Skarsind.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by the senator for Karov, the motion followed a previous motion to relinquish Skarsind. It was passed in principle, with the amount set at 10 thrones. Those 10 thrones were disbursed to the senator for Sermersuaq, ostensibly to ensure the continued Prosperity of the Wintermark citizens affected when Skarsind was given up.

n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are not named, though the motion concerns the Wintermarkers affected by the gifting of Skarsind, the territory they held that season.

t.Skarsind: The Senate allocated 10 thrones, paid to the senator for Sermersuaq, to support the Wintermark citizens affected by the gifting of Skarsind.

Handful of magic.d: Spring magic filled the waters of Redoubt, Spiral and Segura, healing any non-fatal wound almost overnight. Magical storms battered Spiral and Feroz, penalising local fleets by up to a quarter and damaging any navy that started, ended or passed through them. Five more high-lineage briar children were born around Tower March in Upwold, and the first appeared in Mieriada in Miekarova. The thirtieth-magnitude Night fog still clung to the northern Bay of Catazar. Penumbral Veils continued over Madruga, Zenith and Tassato, warping the night skies. In Redoubt the Court of the White Fountain began to crumble under a Winter curse of around magnitude one hundred, its fire plume shrinking by a quarter.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: a curse on the Barrens is noted as Spring-tinged magic and said to have been detailed in the Winds of War.
n.Grendel: Grendel-held Spiral was battered by magical storms that hampered its fleets and damaged passing navies, even as its waters gained Spring healing power; Summer observers also speculated the Catazar fog might be an attack on the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named; Highguard-held Casinea is associated with the lingering Night fog on the northern Bay of Catazar.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: a Summer eminence's servant, Lytemna, is said to be delayed visiting the deCasillon and their Navarr guests.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn saw healing waters in Segura, damaging storms off Feroz, and a powerful Penumbral Veil over Madruga, where the Freeborn Storm fortunately remained docked at the Atalaya shipyards.
n.The League: The night skies over Tassato were warped by a Penumbral Veil, the least potent of the three, which also produced seven strange rainbows during one rainstorm.
n.The Marches: Five more briar children were born in Upwold, mostly around Tower March, making up over half the area's births that season.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Redoubt gained healing Spring waters but its great Court of the White Fountain began to crumble under a Winter curse, while a potent Penumbral Veil continued to shroud Zenith.
n.Varushka: The first eerie briar child was born in Mieriada in Miekarova, and Summer observers noted a Spring aura over the forests of central Varushka.

t.Bay of Catazar: The glowing thirtieth-magnitude Night fog still mired the northern bay, concealing even its own nature from Imperial magicians.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named, but is associated with the lingering Night fog on the northern Bay of Catazar.
t.Feroz: Magical storms lashed the Feroz coast, cutting the effectiveness of local fleets by up to a quarter and damaging any navy that began, ended or passed through the territory.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: a Summer eminence notes two of 'That Damn Woman's' fortresses in Kahraman, effects detailed in the Winds of War.
t.Madruga: A Penumbral Veil with a magnitude in the high forties made Madruga's night skies entirely unnatural, including a seemingly destroyed moon, and blocks divination of the territory; the Freeborn Storm stayed safely docked at Atalaya.
t.Miekarova: Shortly after the Winter Solstice the first briar child appeared in Miekarova, in Mieriada.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt's waters healed almost any wound overnight, but the Court of the White Fountain fell under a Winter curse of around magnitude one hundred, crumbling its walls and weakening its fire plume.
t.Segura: Powerful Spring magic filled Segura's waters, healing any non-fatal wound practically overnight.
t.Spiral: Spiral's waters gained healing Spring power while magical storms battered its coast, penalising local fleets and damaging navies passing through.
t.Tassato: A Penumbral Veil, the weakest of three but still impressive, altered Tassato's night skies, produced seven strange rainbows and hinders scrying of the territory.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: a curse on the Barrens is noted as Spring-flavoured magic, detailed in the Winds of War.
t.Upwold: Five more high-lineage briar children were born in Upwold, supernaturally healthy with emerald eyes and patches of bark.
t.Zenith: A Penumbral Veil of low-thirties magnitude continued to distort Zenith's night skies and block divination.

r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Mieriada saw its first briar child born after the Winter Solstice, the phenomenon spreading from distant Tower March.
r.Redoubt/Optarion: The Court of the White Fountain in the foothills of Optarion began crumbling under a Winter curse, its plume of liquid fire losing perhaps a quarter of its height.
r.Upwold/Tower March: Most of the new briar children were born around Tower March, over half of the area's births in the season.

Of tribute.d: The boons went to many claimants. The Royal Houses of Dawn won the Keeper of Tharim's Throne for Gui de Lusignan. The Hierro of Segura won food for their territory and Agramant's Cruel Blessing against Baroness Jaqueline duMoi in Kalino, which creates a difficult legal situation. A grim legion strode to Liaven's Glen to slay the Jotun. Axos claimed the Destruction of the Walls against the Court of the Fountain and a dream-plaguing hunt against Gabriel Barossa and the Wolves of War. Zamashka, Prince of Votika, a powerful Jarmish magician-prince, won several gifts, including ten more years of life. Tharim, the Bound King, judged the Solstice a success. Some boons have already taken effect and others will follow.

n.Dawn: The Royal Houses of Dawn won the boon of the Keeper of Tharim's Throne, and Gui de Lusignan is named as the chosen of Tharim.
n.Grendel: Grendel faces two hostile boons. Skathe's Vengeance will be directed at High Lady Suriad, Salt Lord of Dubhtraig, and the Raging Fire of Surut will fall on the enemies of the Masters of the High Peaks in Grendel-held Spiral.
n.Jotun: A grim legion fighting in the name of the tribes of Kallavesi and Suaq has strode forth to Liaven's Glen to slay the Jotun.
n.The Brass Coast: The sons and daughters of Naguerro and Hierro won food for an entire territory, to be delivered to Segura, and Agramant's Cruel Blessing. Their claim on a boon from Agramant creates a difficult legal situation.
n.Urizen: The descendants of the Sorcerer-Kings won the Destruction of the Walls, to fall on the Court of the Fountain in Redoubt at their command. This is a grave concern given that Axos was thought to be somewhat friendly to the Empire.

t.Kalino: The Cruel Blessing of Agramant, claimed by the sons and daughters of Naguerro and Hierro, is to fall on Baroness Jaqueline duMoi, general of the Wolves of Kobol, in Kalino.
t.Redoubt: The Court of the Fountain in Redoubt is threatened by the Destruction of the Walls, a boon won by the descendants of the Sorcerer-Kings.
t.Segura: The people of Hierro in Segura are to receive enough food to fill the bellies of an entire territory, with the blessings of Agramant.
t.Spiral: The Raging Fire of Surut, won by the Masters of the High Peaks, is to fall on their enemies in Spiral.

Reclaimers.d: Three decades of Druj occupation, the war to expel them and a year of rampaging trees left Holberg in ruins, cutting its taxation. For Holmauer, Piet Van Holberg proposed a clearance and triumphal arch drawing pilgrims, while Katarzyna Von Carstein proposed a park and civic rebuilding that would enrich local businesses. Doing nothing would leave the ruins permanent. Brechtje Van Holberg proposed fearsome new walls for Holmauer, and Menno Van Ritsjhof proposed vastly enlarging Holfried's fortifications to make them the Empire's biggest. A now-unavailable option offered either restoring the dykes of Rebeshof and Ennerlund or letting the Morass reclaim them for herbs. Unnatural briars in Misericorde and Utterlund could impede large armies.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: in the fiction, an investigator notes that the Towerjacks are now in Dawn.
n.Druj: The Druj had been driven from Holberg, but their occupation and destruction of its walls, dykes and suburbs drove these proposals, and Holbergers expected them to return one day.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the proposed triumphal arch in Holmauer was said to rival some of the most impressive architecture in Highguard.
n.The League: League citizens in Holberg were offered competing great works to clear ruins, restore taxation, rebuild the city's famed fortifications and shape the territory's herb production, with the city's pride and prosperity at stake.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: in the fiction, Jonas Quayle still carries an Upwold accent after years in Holberg.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: letting the Morass spread was said to create marshes that could rival Kallavesa's for healing herbs.

t.Holberg: Holberg lay damaged throughout with reduced taxation, and its citizens proposed clearing Holmauer's ruins, building formidable new walls at Holmauer and Holfried, and dealing with the returning Morass, while unnatural briars choked its northern forests.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: its marshes were the benchmark a re-expanded Holberg Morass might rival for valuable healing herbs.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Jonas Quayle's accent is noted as being from Upwold.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The Morass was spreading back into Ennerlund after the Druj destroyed its dykes; a now-unavailable option offered either restoring them or letting it become marsh, raising the upkeep of the Great Pits of Ennerlund.
r.Holberg/Holfried: Holfried's walls still stood, and Menno Van Ritsjhof proposed raising them to a strength of 12,000 within a year to make them the biggest fortification in the Empire.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: The worst-hit region, Holmauer's suburbs lay in vermin-ridden ruins with shattered walls; rival plans proposed an arch, a park-filled rebuilding or inaction, and Brechtje Van Holberg proposed deadly new defences inflicting extra casualties on attackers.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Unnatural vines and briars grew stronger in Misericorde's northern forests, where scattered orc bands avoided Imperial troops, threatening to impede any large-scale army movement.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: Rebeshof lost its fortifications and its farmland was devastated, while the Morass crept in to drown estates; the now-unavailable herbs option would have either restored its dykes or turned it to marsh.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: Utterlund's northern forests remained under a sinister atmosphere, with unnatural briars that could significantly impede campaign armies.

Refusal of the ceding of territories to.d: The Hierro Clan laid claim to two Freeborn territories, Segura and Feroz. In response, the Senate passed a motion proposed by the senator for Madruga and seconded by the senator for Semmerholm, stating plainly that the Empire would not surrender either territory to the Hierro. The page records the motion as having passed, making the Senate's stance on the claim clear. It does not record what the Hierro did in response.

n.The Brass Coast: The Senate refused to give up two of the Freeborn's own territories to the Hierro Clan, affirming that Segura and Feroz would remain part of the Brass Coast and the Empire.

t.Feroz: Feroz was one of the two territories claimed by the Hierro Clan, and the Senate formally refused to surrender it.
t.Segura: Segura was claimed by the Hierro Clan alongside Feroz, and the Senate passed a motion refusing to cede it.

Seven lords of virtue.d: Lady Madrianna of the Blue Stones made the request on the Plenum's behalf, with the priests Hueva Joãon, Caesli Onorato and Olybrius Pancratius. It was Asavea's third attempt and first formal one. The Asaveans would build a minor or major temple in a coastal Bay of Catazar region with their own white granite, local paid labour and free staff. The Empire could then build a temple of similar size in Nemoria, needing 10 or 20 wains of white granite plus Thrones, which the Joãon family offered to waive. Either the Senate or a civilian commissioner could act. Building the temples would improve diplomacy, trade in gloaming and orichalcum, and create liaison roles.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but the Asaveans would only build in the Sarvos regions if that territory, then held by Grendel, returned to Imperial hands.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Asaveans said they would prefer to avoid building their temple in Highguard's Necropolis.
n.The Brass Coast: Most of the proposed sites for the Asavean temple lie in the Brass Coast's Feroz and Madruga, with Siroc Plains the Asaveans' particular preference. That makes the nation central to where the temple and its trade benefits might be based.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the League's Sarvos regions of Bocche, Uccelini and especially Cigno would be acceptable sites, but only if Sarvos were back in Imperial hands.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Naris, in Redoubt, was named as one of the coastal regions where the Asaveans would be willing to build their temple.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Asaveans asked to build their temple in a coastal region on the Bay of Catazar, which would bring better trade with Nemoria for Imperial ships.
t.Feroz: Three of Feroz's regions, Cazar Straits, Fontargenta and Oranseri, were listed as suitable sites for the proposed Asavean temple.
t.Madruga: Madruga offered several suitable sites, and its Siroc Plains was the Asaveans' especially favoured location for their temple.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the Asaveans said they would prefer to avoid building their temple in Necropolis.
t.Redoubt: Naris in Redoubt was named as one of the regions where the Asaveans would accept building their temple.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos was then held by Grendel and the League. The Asaveans would build in Bocche, Uccelini or ideally Cigno only if the territory returned to Imperial hands.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Cazar Straits was listed as a suitable coastal site for the proposed Asavean temple.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Fontargenta was listed as a suitable coastal site for the proposed Asavean temple.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Oranseri was listed as a suitable coastal site for the proposed Asavean temple.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: Calvos Sound was listed as a suitable coastal site for the proposed Asavean temple.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Free Landing was listed as a suitable coastal site for the proposed Asavean temple.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: Lightsea was listed as a suitable coastal site for the proposed Asavean temple.
r.Redoubt/Naris: Naris was the one Urizeni region the Asaveans named as a suitable site for their temple.
r.Sarvos/Bocche: Bocche would be an acceptable temple site, but only if Sarvos were back in Imperial hands.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: Cigno was the Asaveans' ideal site in Sarvos, should the territory return to Imperial hands.
r.Sarvos/Uccelini: Uccelini would be an acceptable temple site, but only if Sarvos were back in Imperial hands.

Snow and rain.d: Blizzards cut off northern communities, some kept alive only by Navarr stridings, while food shortages from the failed Marcher harvest made matters worse. Skarsind fared worst. Divination revealed Naeve's Twisting Blight, which halved farm production, but Winterfolk and Imperial Orcs set aside their quarrel to endure it together. The thaw swelled the Vassa and Scorrero, threatening floods and killing several net riggers. Some scholars blamed widespread Spring magic and talked of urging the Conclave to restrict weather enchantments. More ilium washed down the Scorrero, giving the Bourse seat holder an opportunity to invest more in the Scorrero Nets. Heavy rain from magic could still burst the Vassa and flood Tassato.

n.Highguard: Highguard's lands felt the cold, with heavy snow in Bastion and light flurries in Casinea and Necropolis.
n.Imperial Orcs: The orcs' first winter in their new home of Skarsind was atrocious, worsened by a Winter curse that halved its farms' production, though they worked alongside the Winterfolk to survive.
n.Jotun: Jotun-held Mournwold saw heavy snow and holds the swollen headwaters of the Vassa, where storms or river rituals could cause flooding or farm effects downstream.
n.Navarr: Navarr stridings ferried food and necessities to cut-off communities, and Hercynia was battered by blizzards.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast felt only poor weather and tightened belts, but the swollen Scorrero threatened Segura's net riggers, several of whom died, and storms there could hurt businesses in Segura and Madruga.
n.The League: League lands along the Vassa braced for floods with sandbags, cellars in Tassato were flooded, and its dramaturgists responded with black-humoured plays about Vassa.
n.The Marches: The Marches were still feeling the failed harvest, and the Synod urged Marcher farmers to sell their surplus cheaply through Martin Orchard, who is likely to find a cool welcome on Marcher farms.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: a Navarr character recalls the fimbulwinter the Thule sent before their attack on Skarsind.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the mountains of Urizen saw poor weather, tightened belts and unseasonably cold winds.
n.Varushka: Angry blizzards raged across Varushka's Volodmartz and Miekarova, adding to a harsh winter in the north.
n.Wintermark: Sermersuaq was struck by blizzards, and in Skarsind the native Winterfolk joined the Imperial Orcs in enduring the frigid months.

t.Bastion: Bastion saw heavy snowfalls during the harsh winter.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea saw light flurries of snow.
t.Hercynia: Angry blizzards raged across Hercynia, and its Navarr worried about the snow coming down the mountains in the Spring.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman saw light snow and holds the deep Scorrero. Heavy rain there could damage the Scorrero Nets, while river rituals there would affect farms downstream in Segura and Madruga.
t.Madruga: Madruga's business owners could suffer if storms struck the Scorrero. The Spider's Dream crossing from Madruga to Sarvos could be damaged by a severe Vassa flood.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova was battered by angry blizzards.
t.Mournwold: Mournwold had heavy snow and holds the swollen Vassa headwaters. Magical storms there would likely make the Vassa burst its banks and flood Tassato.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis saw light flurries of snow.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos's farms and herb gardens along the Vassa would gain or suffer from river rituals upstream, and its Spider's Dream crossing could be damaged by severe flooding.
t.Segura: The swollen Scorrero threatened Segura, killing several net riggers but loosening extra ilium for the Scorrero Nets, and storms could damage the nets and local businesses.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq was struck by angry blizzards that left isolated communities cut off.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind endured an atrocious, curse-blighted winter that halved farm production, forcing farmers to open their stockpiles while Winterfolk and orcs worked together to survive.
t.Tassato: The Vassa ran dangerously high through Tassato, flooding cellars. Heavy rain could flood the city, harm personal resources and damage the Sapphire Stair locks.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Martin Orchard, chosen to tackle the food shortages, is a monk of Pickham Monastery in Upwold.
t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz was battered by angry blizzards.

r.Hercynia/Northpines: Mentioned in passing: in the story, Navarr fear the snow piled on the Northpines will come down in Spring, and some Pridestalkers talk of triggering an avalanche deliberately.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: The region is not named on the page. It is tied to Segura's swollen Scorrero, which brought flood risk and deaths among net riggers but also extra ilium for the Scorrero Nets.
r.Tassato/Cascatas: The region is not named on the page. It is tied to Tassato's swollen Vassa, where flood defences were raised and cellars flooded, with the threat of the river bursting its banks.

Some to misery are born.d: With the Tassato Chamber of Commerce's approval, the Whittle folk fairly bought two streets in Tassato Mestra, opened a bakery and a pub, and kept their streets clean, safe and well maintained. They held a vigil for kin who died at Overton, celebrating twenty thousand dead Jotun. Angered by Friar Robin's execution for blasphemy, they drove off visiting Marcher priests, including an Upwold monk. The League assembly could denounce them as blasphemers, ending the Chamber's green iron arrangement and likely forcing them out by year's end, possibly violently. The Marcher assembly could instead have Upwold, Mitwold and Bregasland shun them, denying them trade and sanctuary.

n.Jotun: The Jotun are the object of the Whittle folk's Hatred, which they credit with thirty years of resistance, and their vigil celebrated the twenty thousand Jotun dead at Overton.
n.The League: The League hosts the Whittle enclave in Tassato, and its national assembly has the option of a mandate denouncing the newcomers as blasphemers, which would end the Chamber of Commerce's profitable arrangement with them and risk violence.
n.The Marches: The Marcher assembly, which executed Friar Robin and condemns Hatred, could pass a mandate to have the Whittle folk shunned as not being good Marchers. Its visiting priests have been driven out of the enclave by the angry Whittle folk.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland is one of the three Marcher territories where a proposed Marcher assembly mandate would urge people to shun the Whittle folk, refusing them trade and sanctuary.
t.Mitwold: Under the proposed Marcher assembly mandate, the people of Mitwold would shun the Whittle folk and refuse them trade or sanctuary if they were driven from Tassato.
t.Mournwold: The Whittle folk left the Mournwold after resisting a thirty-year Jotun occupation there. Many of their young people died defending Overton and Orchard's Watch when it fell, and the Drakes were praised for refusing to cede an inch of the territory.
t.Tassato: Tassato's Chamber of Commerce welcomed the Whittle enclave and shares in its green iron. However, a possible League assembly mandate would turn the enclave into a shunned ghetto and probably drive its people out by year's end.
t.Upwold: An Upwold monk was forcibly driven from the enclave for preaching against Hatred, and Upwold is named among the territories where a proposed mandate would have the Whittle folk shunned.

r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: The Whittle folk bought two streets in Tassato Mestra and opened a bakery and a pub there. Those streets are now perhaps the cleanest and best-lit in the city, but they are at the centre of the Synod's dispute over Hatred.

Strange fruit.d: The Synod had supported Duke Ferrero preaching tolerance of the refugee Hierro and Elka Nadyanova Gremani guiding them using the example of the Paragon of Kethry. Influential Lasambrians such as Kenza began extolling the Virtues to their own people, even confronting bandit warlords. Priests reported that the conversion of thousands was widespread and heartfelt, the greatest since the Empire's founding or the integration of the Imperial Orcs. The Hierro did not adopt the Way exactly, rejecting reincarnation and the Labyrinth, but reached a compromise around the Virtues. Quarrels with Segura's Freeborn almost stopped, yet all agreed the Lasambrians could not stay there forever. The Civil Service offered no suggestions on their future.

n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the integration of the Imperial Orcs is cited as the last conversion comparable to that of the Lasambrians.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are named as the enemy who defeated the Hierro in battle and to whom the other Lasambrian orcs had sold out.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn, long robbed by Lasambrian bandits, admitted that something extraordinary had been achieved, and their quarrels with the refugees all but ceased. They still agreed the Lasambrians could not remain among them forever.

t.Segura: The Hierro refugees sheltering in Segura embraced the Virtues, and calls to drive them off or kill them died away. Even so, Segura's people agreed the Lasambrians could not stay there permanently, leaving their future for the Empire to decide.

The Courageous Priest.d: Golan preached across Reikos that the First Empress was an exemplar of Courage and that the Empire must embrace Courage alone. Nina's Synod-backed campaign was wise but lacked resources, and the Synod had not refuted the claim about the Empress's Courage. Yael's presence drew as many pilgrims to Courage as Golan did. Every Courage congregation in Highguard gained liao and votes, and all others lost them. Golan has been called to inquisition at the Spring Equinox. A General Assembly judgement refuting the Empress's Courage, backed by liao, could halt or reverse the movement. Supporting judgements could spread it to further territories in several nations.

n.Dawn: Astolat could be affected if the Synod backs Golan's claims, and Semmerholm and Weirwater could follow in a wider second spread of the Courage of the First Empress.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: in the accompanying fiction, the Druj are described as scattered and defeated as the liberation of Reikos nears completion.
n.Highguard: The Courage of the First Empress has spread to every corner of Highguard. Courage congregations there are swelling with liao and votes while congregations of every other virtue are losing both, and families are being divided over the movement.
n.Navarr: Miaren and Therunin are among the first territories the movement could spread to if the Synod endorses Golan's teaching or recognises the First Empress as an exemplar of Courage.
n.The Brass Coast: Madruga and Feroz could be affected in a second, wider spread of the Courage of the First Empress if the Synod chooses to promote it further.
n.The League: Sarvos and Tassato are first in line to be affected if the movement spreads beyond Highguard, and Temeschwar could follow later. A Leaguer, Vitória Barossa di Tassato Regario, raised the judgement putting Golan's inquisition in the hands of the Courage Assembly.
n.The Marches: Upwold could be reached by the Courage of the First Empress in a second spread, if the Synod recognises the First Empress as an exemplar of Courage and then commits further liao.
n.Urizen: Morrow and Redoubt are among the first territories the movement could spread to if the Synod gives its backing to Golan's claims.
n.Varushka: Karov could be affected in a second, wider spread of the Courage of the First Empress if the Synod chooses to extend it.

t.Astolat: Astolat is named as one of the first territories the movement could reach, if the Synod supports Golan's claims with 75 liao or recognises the First Empress as an exemplar of Courage.
t.Feroz: Feroz could see the movement's effects in a second spread, after a recognition of the First Empress's Courage and a further 75 liao from the Courage Assembly.
t.Karov: Karov is listed among the territories the movement could reach in a second spread, if the Synod chooses to extend it further.
t.Madruga: Madruga could be affected in the second wave of the movement's possible spread, should the Synod recognise the Empress's Courage and commit more liao.
t.Miaren: Miaren is among the first territories that would feel Golan's teaching if the Synod endorses his claims or recognises the First Empress as an exemplar of Courage.
t.Morrow: Morrow could see congregations of Courage swell at others' expense if the Synod's backing spreads Golan's teaching into the first wave of territories.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt is named among the first territories to which the Courage of the First Empress could spread with Synod support.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Reikos, the territory where Golan, Nina and Yael preached, is not among the territories listed for this entry.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos is among the first territories the movement could reach if the Synod gives its support to Golan's claims or recognises the Empress's Courage.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm could be reached in a second spread of the movement, after a recognition of the First Empress's Courage and a further 75 liao.
t.Tassato: Tassato is named among the first territories the Courage of the First Empress could spread to if the Synod backs it.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar is listed among the territories the movement could reach in a second, wider spread.
t.Therunin: Therunin could see Golan's teaching take hold in the first wave of spread, should the Synod back his claims.
t.Upwold: Upwold could be affected in the second wave of the movement's possible spread if the Synod chooses to extend it.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater is among the territories the Courage of the First Empress could reach in a second spread with further Synod support.

The sack of Sarvos.d: Grendel ships landed thousands of Broken Shore soldiers, crushing armed resistance. Civilians who cooperate are largely left alone, but harming an invader means enslavement in the southern salt mines, and laying hands on a Grendel means execution. The orcs looted Diora University, Capodomus Cathedral and even the tomb of Empress Giselle, shipping treasures to the Broken Shore. Resource production would be halved if occupation continued, and Imperial taxation suffered, partly permanently. The Synod or League assembly could call the people to rise up, backed by the Mayor of Caricomare; Vitória Barossa provided 25 liao. The Grendel are seizing builders and engineers and clearing ground near the quayside, apparently for a major construction project.

n.Grendel: Grendel forces from the Broken Shore seized Cigno, looted its treasures for shipment home, enforced brutal martial law and began rounding up architects and engineers, apparently for a major building project on the island.
n.The League: The League suffered a grievous blow to its pride and wealth as one of its greatest cities was occupied and pillaged, including the tomb of Empress Giselle; its national assembly was given the opportunity to call the citizens of Sarvos to armed uprising.

t.Sarvos: Sarvos faced halved resource production if Grendel occupation persisted, a significant and partly permanent loss of taxation to the Imperial Treasury, and the prospect of a bloody popular uprising that could inflict heavy casualties on the occupiers but provoke retaliation.

r.Sarvos/Cigno: Cigno, home of the city proper, was conquered; its university, cathedral and imperial tomb were looted, the partly built Caricomare cargo dock was stripped bare, and civilian labour gangs were forced to flatten ground near the quayside.

Up on Whittle Hill.d: With the Imperial advance in the Mournwold stalled by the Jotun defence, scouts from the army of the Tusks reached Whittle, at the foot of Whittle Hill in Freemoor. After a brief Jotun occupation, the villagers had retaken their land and waited three decades for help. They grudgingly quartered Imperial troops and showed marked hostility to lineaged soldiers, but declared themselves loyal to the Empire and had kept Marcher traditions such as their yearly fayres. With no liao for thirty years, they were eager to reconnect with their faith. They resolved to send representatives to Anvil, hinted at a hidden treasure, possibly a rich vein of ore, that they might sell, and might offer further unspecified support to the liberation.

n.Jotun: Jotun patrols that usually watched the Whittle valley had been called away, and the village proved to be an enclave that had resisted them for thirty years. The villagers wanted to discuss how to drive the Jotun out of Freemoor.

t.Mournwold: Although the Imperial campaign to liberate the Mournwold had stalled against the Jotun defence, contact with Whittle opened a possible new source of support and a sign of Marcher resilience within the Jotun-held territory.

r.Mournwold/Freemoor: Imperial scouts reached Freemoor and found Whittle still held by its Marcher folk. The villagers offered a possible ore discovery beneath Whittle Hill and planned to send envoys to Anvil to discuss ousting the Jotun from the region.
